issue_context.title: ENH: skip_blank_columns in read_csv
issue_context.body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem?

If the `names` parameter in `read_csv` has more elements than the number of columns in the input file, then the returned DataFrame has `NaN` columns for the extra elements.

#### Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `skip_blank_columns` parameter in `read_csv` (similar to `skip_blank_lines`) to avoid creating the `NaN` columns.

#### API breaking implications

An additional parameter in `read_csv` should not break anything.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered

`read_csv` can be followed by `dropna()` to achieve this, but `skip_blank_columns` would complement the `skip_blank_lines` functionality currently in `read_csv`.
comments: Instead of adding a new parameter, I would consider repurposing `drop_blank_lines` to be `drop_blank`, which accepts something like `None`, `row` (or 0), `column` (or 1), or `both`, somewhat akin to an `axis` argument in other functions.
Thanks for the request, but it appears this hasn't gain traction in a while so closing

review_comments: if we end up doing this we will want to put this argument at the end because it's possible (if bad practice) to pass these arguments as positionals
